decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents:&nbsp;<span style="line-height: 115%;">Fire
Safety Statement, Drainage Strategy (October 2026), Flood Risk Assessment
(March 2026), Arboricultural Impact Assessment (dated May 2026), Topographical
Survey TS24-297-1 (dated May 2024), Planning Statement, Sections TS24-297-8
(May 2024), Location Plan As Existing and Site Plan As Proposed TPD-368-000, Existing
Ground Floor Plan TS24-297-2, Existing Elevations TS24-297-7, Existing First
Floor Plan TS24-297-3, Existing Second Floor Plan TS24-297-4, Proposed
Elevations TPD-368-060 REV A, Proposed Sections TPD-368-070, Proposed Plans TPD-368-050
REV A, Heritage Statement (July 2026), Covering Letter (dated 25th August
2026), Preliminary Roost Assessment (4th August 2026), Bat Emergence
Survey Report (Dated September 2025), Bat Activity Survey (6th August
2024), Noise Impact Assessment (dated 14th August 2026), Existing
Roof Floor Space TS24-297-6, Energy Statement (Dated 14th May 2026),
Fire Safety Strategy, Design and Access Statement (Dated May 2026), Existing
Roof Plan TS24-297-5, Tree Survey and Aboricultural Impact Assessment (20th
April 2026).</span>

<p class="CM5" style="margin: 0px 0px 0cm; text-align: justify;"><span lang="EN-US">No site works or development shall commence until details of the levels of the building(s), road(s) and footpath(s) in relation to the adjoining land and highway(s), and any other changes proposed in the levels of the site, have been submitted to, and approved by, the local planning authority.<o:p></o:p></span></p><p><br></p>

<p><span data-teams="true">No construction works shall take place including any works of demolition, until a Construction Method Statement&nbsp; has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The Method Statement shall provide for:<br>a) detailed timeline for the phases and implementation of the development</span></p><p><span data-teams="true"><br></span>b) the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors;</p><p><span data-teams="true">c) loading and unloading of plant and materials;<br>d) storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development;<br>e) measures to control the emission of dust and dirt during construction; and<br>f) scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works.</span></p><p><span data-teams="true">g) routes of approach by construction vehicles to and from site&nbsp;</span></p><p><span data-teams="true">h) types of vehicles to be used during the construction process</span></p><p><span data-teams="true"><br>The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Method Statement or any amendment or variation to it as may be agreed in writing by the local planning authority throughout the construction period.</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal">No development shall take place (including vegetation/site clearance) until a Precautionary Working Method Statement (PWMS) for herptiles and nesting birds has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The PWMS should include, but may not be limited to;<o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal"><o:p>&nbsp;</o:p></p><ol start="1" type="i" style="margin-top: 0cm;"><li class="MsoNormal">A toolbox talk covering the ecology of and legislation which protects species which may be present on site, to be delivered to construction personnel by the ECoW;<o:p></o:p></li><li class="MsoNormal">A plan showing areas of sensitivity and exclusion zones;<o:p></o:p></li><li class="MsoNormal">Details of where and how waste and/or construction materials will be stored;<o:p></o:p></li><li class="MsoNormal">Details of mitigation measures required for protected species, such as herptile fencing;<o:p></o:p></li><li class="MsoNormal">Details of which construction tasks pose a risk to protected species, and will therefore be supervised by the ECoW;<o:p></o:p></li><li class="MsoNormal">Measures for supervised vegetation clearance (e.g., phased, directional cut); and<o:p></o:p></li><li class="MsoNormal">Procedures to be followed if a protected species is discovered.<o:p></o:p></li></ol><p class="MsoNormal"><o:p>&nbsp;</o:p></p><p>The approved PWMS shall be implemented in full according to the specified timescales, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority</p>

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any order revoking and re-enacting that order with or without modification), no window(s)/door(s), other than those shown on the approved plans shall be installed in the side elevation(s) of the development hereby permitted without the prior permission in writing of the local planning authority.

The window(s) in the side elevation(s) of the proposed development shall:
(a) be of purpose-made obscure glass,
(b) be permanently fixed closed below a height of 1.7m above finished floor level,
and shall thereafter be retained in that form.

<p><u>Sensitive Timing of Works</u></p><p class="MsoNormal">All site clearance (including the removal of any vegetation
or works to areas sensitive) shall be timed so as to avoid the bird nesting
season, this being during the months of March until September inclusive, unless
the Local Planning Authority has confirmed in writing that such works can
proceed, based on submission of a survey (no more than 48hrs before works
commence) undertaken by a suitably qualified ecologist to assess the nesting
bird activity on site, together with details of measures to protect the nesting
bird interest on the site as required.<o:p></o:p></p>

<p><u>Restricted Lighting&nbsp;</u></p><p class="MsoNormal">No external lighting shall be installed on the dwelling
hereby permitted unless full details of a lighting scheme are submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include
details of the exact location, height, design, and intensity of the lights, and
shall be designed to prevent light spillage onto nearby habitat suitable for
bats. The lighting shall be installed and operated strictly in accordance with
the approved details.<o:p></o:p></p>

<p><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until there has been submitted to, and approved by, the local planning authority, a scheme of hard and soft landscape works for the site including: a) Planting plans (at a scale not less than 1:100) b) Schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes, plant container sizes (all at time of planting) and proposed numbers / densities c) Written specification of planting and cultivation works to be undertaken d) A landscape implementation programme with proposed timing / dates for the works. e) Boundary Treatment f) Landscaping Scheme – Implementation and implementation programme, including a period of 5 year period for replacements of soft landscape g) levels h) details hard landscaping materials to be used for patio and hardstanding i) landscape masterplan&nbsp;</span></p>

<p>All planting, seeding or turfing comprised in the approved details of landscaping shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons following the occupation of the building(s), or the completion of the development, whichever is the sooner. Any existing or new trees or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years from the completion of the development, die, are removed, or become seriously damaged or diseased, shall be replaced in the next planting season, with others of a similar size and species, unless the local authority agrees any variation in writing.</p>

<p class="CM5" style="margin: 0px 0px 0cm; text-align: justify;"><span lang="EN-US">Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 1995 (or any order revoking and re-enacting that order with or without modification), no development in relation to the proposed dwellinghouses which would otherwise fall within Classes A, B, D, E, F and G in Part 1 of Schedule 2, and Class AA of Part 20 of Schedule 2 to that Order shall be carried out without the prior written permission of the local planning authority.<o:p></o:p></span></p><p><br></p>

<p class="CM5" style="margin: 0px 0px 0cm;"><span lang="EN-US">Prior to the first occupation of the development, evidence of Secured by Design Certification shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing to be agreed. Secure by design measures shall be implemented and the development shall be retained in accordance with the approved details.<o:p></o:p></span></p><p><br></p>

<p>The development shall be carried out exactly in
accordance with the Impact Assessment, Tree Survey, Tree Protection Plan and
Method Statement approved (GHA trees report) and subject to pre-arranged
monitoring and supervision by the appointed tree specialist</p>
<p><span data-teams="true">The roof lights hereby approved shall not project more than 0.2m beyond the roof plane and shall be retained as such thereafter.&nbsp;</span></p>

<p><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">Prior to occupation of the dwelling, details of a complete post installation noise test and a vibration verification test under taken to demonstrate compliance with the approved noise and vibration mitigation measures with regard to the four A/C units and ASHP proposed</span><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">&nbsp;shall be submitted and approved by the local planning authority.&nbsp;</span></p>

<p>Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved drawings, the development shall not progress beyond damp proof course level until samples of the materials (or appropriate specification) to be used in the construction of the external surfaces noted below have been submitted to, and agreed in writing by, the local planning authority: </p><p>a) All facing and roof materials for the buildings</p><p> b) Windows/doors/glazing; and</p><p> c) Ridge tile details for the crown roof</p><p> d) external patio and hardstanding materials&nbsp; </p><p>e) soffits and fascia details </p><p>f) cladding or similar to be applied to external walls </p><p><span style="text-align: justify;">g) material details of the A/C units and ASHP enclosures&nbsp;</span></p><p><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details so agreed and shall be retained as such thereafter.&nbsp;</span></p>

<p>The development hereby permitted shall be constructed to the specifications of: "Part M, M4 (2), Category 2: Accessible and Adaptable Dwellings" of the Building Regulations 2013 and thereafter retained in that form.</p>

<p><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">The development other than demolition works, hereby permitted shall not commence until details of a revised drainage strategy, with regard to the separate disposal of surface water and foul water, have been</span><span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">&nbsp;submitted to, and agreed in writing by, the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the works so agreed and the works shall thereafter be retained.</span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><u>Biodiversity Enhancement Plan</u></p><p class="MsoNormal">Prior to the commencement of construction, a scale, colour plan of
biodiversity enhancements on the site, to include the number, specification,
and location of enhancements such as replacement, native tree planting, and
species-specific features shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority. Thereafter, the biodiversity enhancement measures
shall be carried out and retained in accordance with the approved details</p>
The development hereby approved shall provide for a minimum of two cycle spaces. The cycle storage shall be made available prior to occupation and shall be retained thereafter.
